Key role of histone deacetylation mediated by histone deacetylases in maintaining retinal homeostasis and intervention strategies

The key role of histone deacetylation mediated by histone deacetylases in maintaining retinal homeostasis and intervention strategies. (A) SIRT1-mediated protection. SIRT1 deacetylates H3K9ac at the p53-associated p66Shc promoter to repress p66Shc transcription, thereby limiting downstream Rac1/NOX2-dependent ROS generation. In parallel, SIRT1 engages the LKB1/AMPK pathway to restrain PARP activity and oxidative stress, attenuating NF-κB/Bax-linked inflammatory and apoptotic signaling and the persistence of injury consistent with metabolic memory. SIRT1 also counterbalances the histone acetyltransferase p300; disruption of the SIRT1-p300 equilibrium favors pro-permeability and pro-fibrotic outputs (e.g., ET-1, TGF-β, and Collagen I), contributing to vascular leakage. (B) SIRT6 and neurovascular stability. SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9ac and H3K56ac to sustain neurotrophic signaling (BDNF) while repressing pathological angiogenic programs (VEGF). Dysregulation of this axis contributes to neurovascular unit dysfunction and promotes DR progression. (C) Therapeutic strategies. Pharmacological restoration of the NAD⁺-SIRT axis (sirtuin activators and metabolic modulators) is proposed to re-establish deacetylation-dependent protective programs and improve retinal outcomes under diabetic stress. SIRT Sirtuin, p66shc p66 isoform of Src homology 2 domain-containing transforming protein 1, Rac1 ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 1, NOX2 NADPH oxidase 2, ROS reactive oxygen species, LKB1 liver kinase B1, AMPK AMP-activated protein kinase, PARP Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, NF-κB nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells, Bax Bcl-2-associated x protein, ET-1 endothelin-1, TGF-β transforming growth factor-beta, BDNF brain-derived neurotrophic factor, VEGF vascular endothelial growth factor, HDAC histone deacetylase
